title: Meter anomaly alerts — design notes (draft)
content:
Context / why
- Finance + RevOps need confidence that billed units are explainable and that we catch issues before invoices go out.
- We now have (or are adding) daily reconciliation (ENG-4821 / PR 41872) and improved export schema (PR 41966). This doc focuses specifically on anomaly dashboards + alert routing (ENG-4824 / obs-pack PR 992).
- Primary consumers: #finance, #eng-sre oncall, telemetry/metering engineers.

Non-goals (for this doc)
- Not selecting a full ML anomaly product. Keep it simple (rules + baselines) with clear suppression controls.
- Not rebuilding metering pipelines.

Definitions (quick)
- Raw telemetry aggregate: sum of metering events emitted by API gateway / runtime (source-of-truth-ish) grouped by day/customer/meter/model/region.
- Billing-ready aggregate: post-transform aggregate used for invoice line items (applies rounding rules, eligibility, exclusions, contract mapping, etc.).
- Delta: billing_ready - raw_telemetry (after aligning dimensions/timezones).
- “Invoice run”: a specific invoicing job execution (invoice_run_id). During reruns/backfills we expect temporary weirdness; alerts must be backfill-aware.

Design principles
1) Alerts should be explainable in <2 minutes (why did this fire, where to click next).
2) Alert payload must include: customer_id/account_name, meter, model, region, env, window_start/end, observed value, baseline/expected, links to dashboard drilldowns and runbook.
3) Prefer detecting upstream anomalies early (missing dims, sudden drops) over only catching invoice deltas late.
4) Suppress during known disruptive operations (backfill, pipeline deploy) but still record for audit.

Alert taxonomy (proposed)
A) Spend spike / usage spike alerts (customer-impact / fraud / misconfig)
B) Negative deltas / reconciliation deltas (billing integrity)
C) Missing or malformed dimensions (pipeline bug)
D) Structural time-series anomalies (sustained drift) vs one-off jitter
E) “Silent failure” (zero usage when historically non-zero)

Routing + severity
- SEV0 (page SRE + notify Finance): evidence of systematic overbilling OR pipeline generating obviously invalid billed units at scale.
- SEV1 (page SRE, notify Finance): large deltas for a single enterprise account, or sustained spike that likely triggers dispute.
- SEV2 (Slack-only): small deltas beyond tolerance, missing dims for low-volume endpoints, dashboard-only follow up.

Proposed routing rules:
- PagerDuty: Eng SRE oncall (SEV0/SEV1). Secondary: Telemetry/Metering (Logan/Nadia) rotation if we set one up; for now tag in Slack.
- Slack channels:
  - #eng-sre (all alerts)
  - #finance (SEV0/1 + selected SEV2 if enterprise/customer-at-risk)
  - #billing-platform-internal (optional; for pipeline owners)

Implementation notes (Grafana/Prometheus vs SQL)
- Reality: most of the metrics live in warehouse tables; easiest is a scheduled query job that writes results to an “anomaly_events” table and then Grafana reads it.
- For fast “pipeline health” (missing dimensions / zero events) we can also use existing Prometheus counters from the metering service.

Data sources (current / planned)
- warehouse.metering.raw_events_daily (or equivalent) — aggregated by day
- warehouse.billing.billing_ready_daily — aggregated by day
- warehouse.billing.invoice_exports — includes meter_version, aggregation_window, invoice_run_id (PR 41966)
- metadata.customer_dim (tier, plan, sales_owner)
- metadata.model_alias_dim (console-alias mapping)

Dashboards (draft links / placeholders)
- Grafana: Metering → Reconciliation Overview
  - https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/meter-recon/meter-reconciliation-overview
- Grafana: Metering → Customer Drilldown
  - https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/meter-cust/metering-customer-drilldown
- Grafana: Metering → Dimension Completeness
  - https://grafana.redwoodinference.internal/d/meter-dims/meter-dimension-completeness
- Looker (Finance): Usage vs Invoice (read-only)
  - https://looker.redwoodinference.internal/looks/usage_vs_invoice

Checks + thresholds (v0)

A1) Customer daily spend spike (hosted API)
- Metric: total_billed_usd_day by customer_id (hosted) OR total_tokens_day by customer_id if USD not available until later stage.
- Baseline: trailing 14d median per customer, with weekday adjustment later.
- Trigger (SEV1):
  - observed > max(3x baseline, baseline + $2,000) for enterprise tier
  - observed > max(5x baseline, baseline + $200) for self-serve
- Trigger (SEV2): observed > 2x baseline and absolute > $50.
- Notes / false positives:
  - Customers doing planned load tests (should be allowlisted temporarily).
  - Model rollout switching to a more expensive model family can appear as “spend spike” even if tokens constant.
  - Backfills can cause double-counted day values if dashboard sums without invoice_run_id filter.

A2) Customer request rate spike
- Metric: requests_day by customer_id + endpoint_type (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank)
- Trigger: > 5x 7d median AND absolute > 10k req/day (tune per endpoint)
- Use case: leaked keys, runaway retries client-side, abusive usage.

B1) Reconciliation delta beyond tolerance (daily)
- Metric: abs(billing_ready_units - raw_units) / raw_units per (customer_id, meter_name, model_family, region) for day D.
- Default acceptance tolerance:
  - tokens: <= 0.5% for high-volume customers (>10M tokens/day), <= 1.5% for medium, <= 3% for low volume (noise/rounding)
  - embeddings/rerank: <= 0.5% (units less jittery)
- Trigger (SEV0):
  - systematic: > 1% delta affecting >= 20 customers OR >= $25k projected month impact
- Trigger (SEV1):
  - single enterprise customer: > 1.5% delta AND absolute delta > $500/day
- Trigger (SEV2):
  - > 3% delta for any customer with absolute delta > $50/day
- Notes:
  - Need to align timezones (billing uses UTC day; console may use account tz). Console alignment work (ENG-4825) reduces noise.
  - Streaming partials: pre-fix can cause “raw > billing” or “billing > raw” depending on where disconnect is recorded. See ENG-4822/PR 41903.

B2) Negative billed units (should never happen)
- Metric: any billing_ready_units < 0 by meter/day
- Trigger: SEV0 immediately
- Likely causes: join duplication with negative adjustments, backfill merge bug.

B3) Invoice export schema regression
- Metric: missing meter_version or aggregation_window or invoice_run_id in invoice export rows
- Trigger: SEV1 (blocks auditability; may block close depending on volume)

C1) Missing critical dimensions rate
- Critical dims:
  - customer_id
  - model_id (or model_alias mapped)
  - region
  - endpoint_type
  - meter_name
  - request_outcome (planned ENG-4823/PR 41917)
- Metric: count(*) where dim is null / total rows
- Trigger:
  - SEV1 if missing_rate > 0.1% sustained 30m OR any spike > 1% in 5m
  - SEV2 if missing_rate > 0.01% in low traffic envs
- Notes:
  - Some older ingestion paths don’t emit request_outcome yet; need “expected missing until backfill” config.

D1) Zero-usage when historically non-zero (silent failure)
- Metric: total raw events or total tokens per (region, endpoint_type, meter_name)
- Trigger:
  - SEV1 if region-wide zero for > 10 minutes during business hours
  - SEV2 if single meter_name zeros unexpectedly for > 30 minutes
- Notes: can also indicate upstream outage; should be correlated with API error rate.

E1) Retry / outcome mix shift (double counting risk)
- Metric: ratio of tokens where retry_reason is not null, by endpoint_type
- Trigger:
  - SEV2 if ratio increases > 2x baseline
  - SEV1 if ratio > 10% for > 30 minutes AND tokens volume high
- Notes:
  - Before ENG-4823, we can approximate via request_id duplication rate, but it’s noisy.

Suppression / backfill handling (very important)
- During backfills (ENG-4826) we expect:
  - temporarily missing partitions (zeros)
  - temporary double-count in “billing_ready_daily” if job is append-only without delete+replace
  - large reconciliation deltas while backfill window is incomplete
- Proposed suppression mechanisms:
  1) Backfill calendar table: warehouse.ops.backfill_windows (start_ts, end_ts, pipeline_name, ticket, owner). Alerts check if window overlaps and downgrade severity to SEV2 unless “negative units”/schema regression.
  2) Label anomalies with invoice_run_id: dashboards default to “latest successful run” not “sum of all runs”.
  3) Deploy freeze window around month-end close: treat anomalies as higher severity in the 72h before invoicing.

Alert payload template (Slack)
Title: [Metering][SEV1] Reconciliation delta 2.3% ($742) — AcmeCo — tokens.output — llama3.1-70b — us-east-1 — 2026-02-10
Body:
- observed_raw_units: ...
- observed_billing_units: ...
- delta_units: ...
- delta_pct: ...
- projected_monthly_usd (rough): ...
- invoice_run_id: ...
- meter_version: ...
- links:
  - Recon dashboard (filtered)
  - Customer drilldown
  - Runbook: Billing discrepancy triage
- notes: backfill_window_match=true/false

Rough queries (warehouse SQL sketches)

Q1: daily reconciliation delta by customer/meter/model/region
- 목적: B1

WITH raw AS (
  SELECT
    day,
    customer_id,
    meter_name,
    model_family,
    region,
    SUM(units) AS raw_units
  FROM warehouse.metering.raw_events_daily
  WHERE day BETWEEN DATEADD('day', -7, CURRENT_DATE) AND CURRENT_DATE
  GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
), billed AS (
  SELECT
    day,
    customer_id,
    meter_name,
    model_family,
    region,
    SUM(units) AS billed_units,
    MAX(invoice_run_id) AS invoice_run_id,
    MAX(meter_version) AS meter_version
  FROM warehouse.billing.billing_ready_daily
  WHERE day BETWEEN DATEADD('day', -7, CURRENT_DATE) AND CURRENT_DATE
  GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(r.day, b.day) AS day,
  COALESCE(r.customer_id, b.customer_id) AS customer_id,
  COALESCE(r.meter_name, b.meter_name) AS meter_name,
  COALESCE(r.model_family, b.model_family) AS model_family,
  COALESCE(r.region, b.region) AS region,
  r.raw_units,
  b.billed_units,
  (b.billed_units - r.raw_units) AS delta_units,
  CASE WHEN r.raw_units = 0 THEN NULL ELSE ABS(b.billed_units - r.raw_units)/r.raw_units END AS delta_pct,
  b.invoice_run_id,
  b.meter_version
FROM raw r
FULL OUTER JOIN billed b
  ON r.day=b.day
 AND r.customer_id=b.customer_id
 AND r.meter_name=b.meter_name
 AND r.model_family=b.model_family
 AND r.region=b.region;

Q2: missing dimension rate (raw events)
- 목적: C1

SELECT
  DATE_TRUNC('hour', event_ts) AS hour,
  SUM(CASE WHEN customer_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*)::float AS missing_customer_id_rate,
  SUM(CASE WHEN model_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*)::float AS missing_model_id_rate,
  SUM(CASE WHEN region IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*)::float AS missing_region_rate,
  SUM(CASE WHEN endpoint_type IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*)::float AS missing_endpoint_rate
FROM warehouse.metering.raw_events
WHERE event_ts >= DATEADD('day', -1, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1 DESC;

Q3: negative billed units
- 목적: B2

SELECT *
FROM warehouse.billing.billing_ready_daily
WHERE units < 0
  AND day >= DATEADD('day', -30, CURRENT_DATE)
LIMIT 1000;

Known false positives / noise sources (capture as we learn)
1) Backfill windows (see suppression section). Biggest source of alert fatigue.
2) Console vs invoice mismatches due to:
   - timezone normalization differences
   - model alias mapping (console groups; invoice uses canonical model_id)
   - rounding policy differences (ADR says aggregate-level rounding; per-request rounding removal in PR 41888)
3) Streaming disconnect accounting (pre PR 41903): raw may include tokens after client disconnect, or billed may have partials handled differently.
4) Retries double-counting on a single endpoint (noted in Slack #eng). Until request_outcome/retry_reason lands, anomaly checks need to be less sensitive.
5) Low volume customers: delta_pct is unstable. Use absolute thresholds and minimum volume gates.

Actionability / playbooks (who does what)
- When B1 fires for a specific customer:
  1) SRE checks: does it coincide with deploy/backfill? verify invoice_run_id filter.
  2) Telemetry owner checks: join duplication? missing dims? compare raw vs billed queries.
  3) Finance checks: is the account in invoice preview window? should we hold invoice? (per close checklist / Emily)
  4) If customer-facing risk: create Jira support/internal ticket and link evidence.
- When A1/A2 fires:
  1) Check API auth logs / key usage; notify Support/CS if enterprise.
  2) If suspected leak: recommend key rotation and enable rate limits.

Open questions
- Where does “invoice_run_id is authoritative” live? (Ethan/Cole discussion). Need a single owner service and naming convention.
- Do we want per-customer allowlists/expected spikes (e.g., weekly batch job)? If yes, store in metadata.customer_alert_overrides.
- Should Finance receive all SEV2 in #finance or only enterprise tiers? leaning: only enterprise + any SEV2 that touches reconciliation deltas > $50.
- Month-end policy: at what threshold do we block invoicing? (Finance to define; Engineering to implement alert -> checklist gating.)

Next steps (near-term)
- [Allison] finalize v0 thresholds with Finance (Emily/Rishi) and add to ENG-4824 acceptance criteria.
- [Logan/Nadia] confirm table names + dimensionality availability (request_outcome timeline).
- [SRE] implement suppression via backfill_windows table + label in alert payload.
- [Chloe] confirm console alignment changes don’t break dashboards (ENG-4825).

Appendix: contact list (for alert annotations)

(End — draft, expect edits after first week of running alerts in prod.)
